newsitem.title: USA: Generations battle over MTV in Texas town.
newsitem.headline: Generations battle over MTV in Texas town.

text.p: An old-timers' bid to pull the plug on MTV in this small Texas town has sparked a generational battle with its young music fans.

Upset by sexual innuendo and raw language on the MTV cable music video channel, 650 Albany residents signed a petition asking that it be dropped from the local cable line-up. TCI Cablevision recently agreed to replace it with the Christian-oriented Trinity Broadcasting Network on Sept. 1.
But now a group of teenagers and some of Albany's more easy-going adults say MTV is getting a bad rap, and have gathered 400 signatures on a counter-petition asking that it be left right where it is.
Joyce Knight launched the anti-MTV drive after seeing her grandchildren watch the channel.

"They became disrespectful," she said in a telephone interview Tuesday. "My grandson was acting like Beavis and Butthead (an MTV show featuring two rebellious adolescent cartoon characters). When his mother found out that's what he was watching she stopped it and he did a complete turnaround."
Other residents of this town of 1,900 people near Abilene, however, say MTV is a lot cleaner than some of the other cable channels on offer.

"I have yet to see a nude person or a sex scene on MTV, or anything promoting drug use," said Terra Wade, a 17-year-old varsity cheerleader and church volunteer who is coordinating efforts to keep MTV on the air.
"They can't tell my parents what they can allow me to watch and what they can't allow me to watch," Wade said.
TCI's area general manager Raymond Greenwood said he would revisit the issue when he receives the new petition but that it was unlikely the decision to drop MTV would be reversed quickly.
"As a business, we have to try to respond to the community's wants and needs," he said.
